title: Context.dev: how angry emails and free credits grew an API startup to 400 customers
summary: Yahia Bakour explains how furious emails from big customers told him which of several stalled projects to double down on, and how he grew Context.dev to 400 customers in a year and a half. He covers free-credit onboarding, fixing one angry user at a time, and running a four-person team with agents on eval and monitoring loops.

principles.text: Treat angry, detailed customer emails as a product-market fit signal and use them to pick which project to focus on.
principles.quote: why did this person care so much or care enough to write this long email? That means there's probably something here.

principles.text: When several projects stall at the same revenue level, kill the rest and double down on the one.
principles.quote: you need to pick what to double down on cuz you can't just work on a bunch of things at once.

principles.text: Win the first customers by fixing things for the most upset user one at a time.
principles.quote: you just make one person happy at a time cuz people ask for different things.

principles.text: Offer free credits instead of paywalling at the start: churn is lower and you get feedback from people who tried it.
principles.quote: just doing a free free trial or like free credits at the beginning, like a certain amount of credits when they run out you subscribe and then get the constant renewals, that works best

principles.text: Product-led growth is slow at first, then compounds once you become a default option.
principles.quote: it just takes a while to build some sort of critical mass. And then once you hit it, you just go go like crazy because you kind of become a default option

principles.text: Automate a workflow with agents only after it has been proven manually.
principles.quote: we try to only automate something after it's proven to work like manually.
